about.heroH1Part2: . We're building the engineers who'll build
about.heroLead: Robotics is just the language. The mission is bigger — preparing a generation to invent, design and lead the technology of the next fifty years.
about.heroFooter: Founded November 2025  ·  Tashkent → Panama → MTI in one year
about.manifesto: "For decades, world-class robotics felt like something that happens somewhere else. We're here to change that."
about.associationH2: A national non-profit dedicated to robotics, engineering and STEM.
about.associationP1: We prepare and send Uzbek teams to international competitions — FIRST Global, FIRST Tech Challenge, Teknofest, CanSat, MTI robotics — and run national-scale events like the Startup Fest Robotics Challenge to give every student a stage at home.
about.associationP2: Beyond competitions, we mentor coaches, equip schools, and connect young engineers with universities, industry partners and global STEM programs.
about.trackRecordH2Part1: Greece. Panama. China. Dubai. Turkey. America.
about.trackRecordLead: Each result is a student who walked onto a global stage and proved that where you're from doesn't cap how far you can go.
about.commitment1Title: Open the door for every region
about.commitment1Body: Robotics shouldn't be a Tashkent privilege. We bring world-class STEM events to students across all of Uzbekistan — not just the capital.
about.commitment2Body: We train teams to compete at the very top — Panama, Athens, Houston, MTI, Istanbul. The flag goes higher every year.
about.commitment3Title: Build a generation, not a moment
about.commitment3Body: We mentor coaches, equip schools, and connect young engineers to universities, industry partners and global STEM programs.
about.sfrcKicker: And now — a stage at home
about.sfrcLead: SFRC 2026 is our country's first multi-category robotics championship — four disciplines, custom-built arenas, live scoring, formats borrowed from the best leagues in the world.
about.footerNote: Robotics and Engineering Association of Uzbekistan · Founded November 2025 · Tashkent, Uzbekistan

challenge.heroLead: Every SFRC category is engineered to international standards — built from scratch, scored live, judged with formats borrowed from the top robotics circuits in the world.
challenge.firstsH2Line1: SFRC 2026 isn't a re-run of someone else's playbook.
challenge.first1Body: No public combat robotics event has ever been held in Uzbekistan until SFRC.
challenge.first2Body: First real tournament — group stage and playoffs, not just exhibition robots from one team.
challenge.first3Body: Elevated platforms, RGB underglow, polycarbonate walls, live scoring — built like a real championship.
challenge.closingLead: Want to compete, or learn more about the Robotics and Engineering Association of Uzbekistan? Get in touch through our association.
challenge.footer: Robotics and Engineering Association of Uzbekistan · Tashkent, Uzbekistan · 2026

catA.label: Line Follower
catA.tagline: Autonomous chase on an elevated track with laser timing.

unique.title: Elevated platform with RGB underglow
unique.body: The 5490 × 2745 mm track sits on a ~30 cm raised platform with a WS2812B LED strip running underglow around the perimeter and flashing white on finish.

unique.title: Arduino laser-gate timing
unique.body: Custom laser gates measure start and finish using Arduino micros(). The result shows on a 7-segment display and triggers an RGB flash and Wi-Fi update to the website.

unique.title: Drag Race finals on mirrored tracks
unique.body: Top-4 qualifiers race head-to-head on identical mirrored tracks in a Double Elimination format. One run per match, finish determined visually by judges. Places 1–4 awarded.

unique.title: Real track features
unique.body: Crossroads (diamond shape), a diagonal bridge crossing, and 4–5 U-turn serpentines along the full track. White line 19–25 mm on a black background.

unique.title: 10-second self-recovery rule
unique.body: If a robot leaves the track, it has 10 seconds to return on its own with no penalty. Fail to recover → manually placed behind the line with +20s penalty (one time per attempt). Second slip → attempt disqualified.

format: Level 1 (Qualification): Loop Track, 2 attempts per team, ranked by average time. Top-4 advance.
Level 2 (Finals): Face-to-Face Drag Race on mirrored tracks, Double Elimination, places 1–4 awarded.
Per attempt: maximum 2 minutes, 5-minute window to reach the judge after being called.
Tiebreaker: equal time → compare penalty seconds → extra run.

catB.label: Mini Sumo
catB.tagline: The last robot standing — Yuhkoh wins.
catB.firstBadge: First standardised Mini Sumo championship in Uzbekistan

unique.title: Yuhkoh — complete push-out
unique.body: Victory is awarded only when the opponent is fully pushed out of the ring. The Japanese term Yuhkoh defines the win condition — no points, no judges, no doubt.

unique.title: Mandatory 5-second start delay
unique.body: Every match starts with a 5-second delay after the signal. Strategy and reaction logic, not just being faster off the line. False start → foul; second foul in match → round loss.

unique.title: Three randomised starting positions
unique.body: Face-to-Face, Side-by-Side, or Back-to-Back — judge announces the configuration before each round. A robot has to dominate from every angle.

unique.title: Three-phase tournament with Triangle Duel finals
unique.body: Six groups round-robin → 12-team Single Elimination → Triangle Duel Finals where three finalists fight pairwise (A vs B, B vs C, A vs C). Standings by total wins.

unique.title: Full dohyō stage with Shiro-Tawara and Shikiri
unique.body: 770 mm ring with 2.5 cm white Shiro-Tawara edge, two 2 × 8 cm Shikiri lines 20 cm apart, on a ~50 cm platform with an RGB rainbow strip and 50 cm green zone.

format: Phase 1: Six groups, round-robin, best-of-3 matches per pair.
Phase 2: Top-2 from each group → 12-team Single Elimination → 3 finalists.
Phase 3: Triangle Duel — A vs B · B vs C · A vs C, ranked by total wins. Tiebreaker: Golden Match — first robot out loses.
Match interruptions: clinch > 10s → restart; both stuck 15s → restart; second occurrence → draw.

specs.v: IR · ultrasonic · ToF · encoders · IMU · cameras
Magnets · glue · suction · dangerous combat elements

catC.label: MiniRoboWar
catC.tagline: Three fights. Three ways to win. No finals.

unique.title: No final stage — every fight counts
unique.body: Each robot fights 3 separate matches against random opponents. There is no playoff bracket — the podium is decided by accumulated points across all three fights.

unique.title: Three ways to win
unique.body: KO — push opponent fully out of arena, fight ends immediately. Immobilization — opponent unable to move for 10 seconds. Judges decision — if neither happens within 2 minutes.

unique.title: 5-criteria judge scoring (100 pts)
unique.body: Aggression (20), Control & maneuverability (20), Technical superiority (20), Structural durability (20), Damage on opponent (20). Used when no KO or immobilization occurs.

unique.title: Structurally expandable robots
unique.body: Start size is locked at 20 × 20 × 20 cm, but robots may expand structurally once the fight begins. Weapons, ramps and flippers are allowed up to the 2 kg limit.

unique.title: Circular arena with polycarbonate walls
unique.body: ⌀ 2000 mm battle floor with 1300 mm transparent polycarbonate walls forming a cylinder, on a ~50 cm elevated platform with green zone and 8 cm safety border.

format: Each team fights 3 separate matches against random opponents.
Points: Win = 3, Draw = 1, Loss = 0. Top-3 by total points → podium.
Tiebreaker: more wins → total judge scores across 3 fights → extra deciding fight.
Match length: 2 minutes. Both stand 15 seconds → draw. Stuck at wall 10 seconds → considered immobilized.

specs.v: Clear ON/OFF switch for emergency stop
Explosives · flammables · liquid systems · radio jammers · open HV

catD.label: Robo Football
catD.tagline: Stadium with auto-scored goals and real match flow.
catD.firstBadge: First qualification-based Robo Football tournament in Uzbekistan

unique.title: First proper qualification tournament in Uzbekistan
unique.body: Other local events are exhibition demos — two robots from one team playing each other. SFRC runs a full championship between independent teams.

unique.title: 2 robots + 2 drivers per team
unique.body: Each team fields 2 robots controlled by 2 drivers, plus 1 trainer/coach (18+). Drivers may swap controllers between robots during the match. Coaches cannot intervene during play.

unique.title: IR-beam auto-scoring
unique.body: When the ball crosses the goal line it falls into a collector under the goal where a TCRT5000 / E18-D80NK IR sensor triggers an ESP32. The score posts to the website over Wi-Fi automatically.

unique.title: Goal effects: white flash + sound
unique.body: Each detected goal fires a WS2812B white flash on the platform underglow, a 1000 Hz tone on a PAM8403 speaker, and the score animates on the public display.

unique.title: Real match flow: 2 halves, ET, penalties
unique.body: 2 halves × 2 minutes with a 1-minute break. Tie at full time → 2 minutes of Extra Time with the golden-goal rule. Still tied → penalty shootout.

format: Pre-match: all robots weighed and measured, placed in quarantine.
Tie at full time → 2 minutes Extra Time (golden goal).
No-show: 3 announcements over 2 minutes → team is removed from match.
